rules.quote: Patients whose family income is at or below 100% of the FPL are eligible to receive free care.

application.quote: Accounts turned to bad debt remain eligible for financial assistance consideration as long as the complete application and documentation are submitted prior to 240 days from the date of the initial account statement

eca_not_before.quote: ECA's will not be initiated by Community Hospital or by an outside collection agency acting on behalf of Community Hospital until at least 120 days after the initial guarantor account statement has been mailed.

payment_plan.quote: For patients who qualify for charity and who are cooperating in good faith to resolve their discounted hospital bills, Community Hospital may offer extended payment plans

notes: Policy reserves right to exclude or limit non-urgent services from FAP
Financial assistance is last resort after exploring all other payment options (private insurance, Medicare, Medicaid, CHP, liability, Crime Victims, CICP)
Elective procedures and flat rate procedures including cosmetic, bariatric lithotripsy are not eligible; complications from elective procedures considered case-by-case
Duration of eligibility does not exceed 12 months; hospital may reevaluate if income changes or new hospital care needed
Relatives/guardians may apply for incapacitated or deceased individuals
Income determination uses gross personal and business income per CICP guidelines; includes all household members and legally responsible parties
AGB (Amounts Generally Billed) calculated per IRC 501(r) rules; recalculated annually May 1-April 30
Patient must submit documentation: minimum last year's tax return, last 3 months income, or bank statement with checking/savings/investment balances
Completed applications processed within 30 days; written notification within 30 days of receipt
Applicant denied has right to appeal in writing to Business Office Manager within 30 days of denial receipt
Applicant must provide required information within 14 days of application date; failure may result in denial
Misrepresentation/falsification causes financial assistance to be withdrawn retroactively
Records maintained for at least 7 years
Hospital may use outside agencies to estimate income when documentation lacking
Collections policy: reasonable efforts to determine eligibility before ECA; ECA includes wage garnishments, liens on primary residences, other legal actions
Collection activity suspended during financial assistance review; resumes if partial adjustment, failure to cooperate, or ineligibility
Hospital complies with all federal, state, and local laws
Hospital located at 2351 G Road, Grand Junction, CO 81505
req_uninsured_or_underinsured may leave out a condition: Also requires ineligibility for government programs and inability to pay.
req_ineligible_govt_programs may leave out a condition: Also requires being uninsured or underinsured and unable to pay.
req_unable_to_pay may leave out a condition: Also requires being uninsured, underinsured, and ineligible for government programs.

findings.title: Covers everyone Colorado's Hospital Discounted Care protects

law.source: HCPF Hospital Discounted Care Operations Manual, Mar 31 2026
law.quote: Patients and their households are eligible for Hospital Discounted Care if, during the required screening and application processes, they are determined to: Have a total household income at or below 250% of the Federal Poverty Guidelines (FPG), and Be residents of the State of Colorado.
IF REQUESTED BY THE PATIENT, A HEALTH-CARE FACILITY SHALL SCREEN AN INSURED PATIENT FOR DISCOUNTED CARE

findings.summary: A household of 3 earning $27,000 a year (98.8% of the poverty line), living in Colorado, insured, and not under-insured as the policy defines it is turned away by this requirement: "Patient must be uninsured or underinsured". Colorado law makes them eligible for Hospital Discounted Care.

findings.title: Doesn't require a Medicaid application first

law.quote: DENY DISCOUNTED CARE ON THE BASIS THAT THE PATIENT HAS NOT APPLIED FOR ANY PUBLIC BENEFITS PROGRAM

findings.summary: Two households differ only in whether they applied for Medicaid or other public programs: A household of 3 earning $27,000 a year (98.8% of the poverty line), living in Colorado, uninsured, owing $0 is treated worse than the same household with no Medicaid application. Colorado law says whether they applied for Medicaid or other public programs must not decide discounted care.

findings.title: No collection lawsuits or garnishment before day 182

law.quote: NO MEDICAL CREDITOR COLLECTING ON A DEBT FOR HOSPITAL SERVICES SHALL ENGAGE IN ANY PERMISSIBLE EXTRAORDINARY COLLECTION ACTIONS UNTIL ONE HUNDRED EIGHTY-TWO DAYS AFTER THE DATE THE PATIENT RECEIVES HOSPITAL SERVICES.

law.source: HCPF Hospital Discounted Care Operations Manual, Mar 31 2026
law.quote: begin sending bills beginning 46 days after the patient's date of service or date of discharge

findings.summary: If the first bill goes out on day 46 after care (Colorado allows bills from day 46), the policy's written timeline allows collection actions from day 166. Colorado law bars them until day 182.

clauses.label: 120 days after first statement
clauses.quote: ECA's will not be initiated by Community Hospital or by an outside collection agency acting on behalf of Community Hospital until at least 120 days after the initial guarantor account statement has been mailed.

findings.domain: every first-bill day from day 46 to day 400

review.note: ECAs not until at least 120 days after the first post-discharge statement; no 182-day floor stated.

findings.title: Accepts applications for at least 181 days after care

law.source: HCPF Hospital Discounted Care Operations Manual, Mar 31 2026
law.quote: Patients may complete a screening at any time within at least 181 days after their date of service or discharge, whichever is later

law.source: HCPF Hospital Discounted Care Operations Manual, Mar 31 2026
law.quote: begin sending bills beginning 46 days after the patient's date of service or date of discharge

findings.summary: Proved for the encoded rules: whatever day the first bill goes out (Colorado allows bills from day 46), the application window never closes before day 181 after care.
findings.domain: every first-bill day from day 46 to day 400

findings.title: Insured patients get 45 days after their first post-insurance bill

law.source: HCPF Hospital Discounted Care Operations Manual, Mar 31 2026
law.quote: At least 45 days from the date of the first bill after the patient's insurance adjustment, even if that date falls outside the normal 181-day window.

findings.summary: Proved for the encoded rules: the window always stays open at least 45 days past the first bill.
findings.domain: every first-bill day from day 0 to day 400

findings.title: Payment plans capped at 4% of monthly income, done after 36 payments

law.quote: THE PATIENT IS NOT PAYING MORE THAN FOUR PERCENT OF THE PATIENT'S MONTHLY HOUSEHOLD INCOME ON A BILL FROM A HEALTH-CARE FACILITY
AFTER A CUMULATIVE THIRTY-SIX MONTHS OF PAYMENTS, CONSIDER THE PATIENT'S BILL PAID IN FULL

findings.summary: The policy states no payment-plan terms to check. Colorado's 4% / 36-month limits apply anyway.

findings.title: Application window of 240 days after the first bill (501(r))

law.quote: ends on the later of the 240th day after the date that the first post-discharge billing statement for the care is provided

findings.summary: Proved for the encoded rules: for any first-bill day, applications stay open at least 240 days after it.
findings.domain: every first-bill day from day 0 to day 400

findings.title: No collection actions in the first 120 days after the first bill (501(r))

law.quote: for at least 120 days from the date the hospital facility provides the first post-discharge billing statement for the care

findings.summary: Proved for the encoded rules: collection actions never start sooner than 120 days after the first bill.
findings.domain: every first-bill day from day 0 to day 400

findings.title: Earning less never means getting less help
findings.summary: Inconclusive: 1 of the model's rules were dropped by the quote and meaning checks, so a missing rule may be our error. Z3's case: A household of 3 earning $40,980 a year (150.0% of the poverty line), living in Colorado, uninsured, owing $0, who hasn't applied for Medicaid gets no help; the same household earning more, at 150.00% of the poverty line, gets help (amount not stated). The written income bands leave a gap between them.
